There are two major types of Spam that we see on our site: Advertising Spam and Self-Promotion or Original Content Spam

  • Advertising Spam

This is any kind of post or comment with a link or a reference to another site for sales of products or services. These are not welcomed at all and are generally deleted as soon as they are discovered or reported.

  • Self-Promotion or Original Content Spam

This is a website domain or video channel usually created by the user, whose intent is to share with the Voat Community, which is very cool and we love original content. It becomes 'very not cool' when most or even all that the user links is their own domain or channel without linking other stuff, and makes the community feel like it's being used for hits. In fact, it's so 'not cool', it's in violation of our site's submission guidelines...

Can I submit links to sites I operate? Submitting only links to sites you operate (or are associated with), without submitting other, unrelated links, is considered spamming... To be on the safe side, if you submit 10 links to various subverses on Voat, at most 5 of the 10 submitted links may be to the sites you are associated with.

All spam -whether posts or comments- are subject to deletion and may warrant bans to the domain and/or the user.

How to Report Spam

There is a button below every post and comment called report - if you see something that smells like spam then push that button, mark as spam, and thank you! Janitors and Moderators will review these anonymous spam reports and action will be taken as needed.

Major offenders can be reported here at v/ReportSpammers by making a post to get the Domain reviewed for either a possible ban or a guidelines message to the primary user; this link, Domain Spam Report, is the guiding template for reporting domains and is the most effective for getting spam addressed and stopped on Voat. Is it more secure to sign in to a site every time? Or does that give a potential hacker more opportunity to steal my password?

If signing in is insecure, the browser warns you. If cookies are sent to insecure pages, the site did it on purpose. If you don't receive warnings and the site and sign-in is secure, then a man in the middle has no easy way to attack no matter what you do.

The only possible difference is local: how quickly an attacker who has access to your computer or browser profile can access that account. But normally we have to assume that if they have made it that far, the machine is under their complete control already.

For most websites, I think mass password thefts come from the server side. Even if passwords are not stored in the database verbatim the attacker can change the code to harvest them as people authenticate.

Using existing keys/sessions reduces that possibility slightly, but realistically they are going to get your password just by terminating your session and forcing you to enter your password again.
